status: Router given an opt-in water cost, verified. Gullfjellstoppen routed down to 1,18% of its length on water, from a line that ran a kilometre along Osavatnet. Guide not written.
note: Gullfjellstoppen is researched, corridored and routed, and is held back by one decision recorded under its findings: the router puts the line on lake ice, by design, and that design does not transfer to a coastal tour starting at 307 m with a regulated lake on the way. Nothing from this file is in lib/tours.ts, lib/routes.ts or lib/guides.ts.
why: Bergen is the largest hole in the map. The nearest tour in the app is Vesoldo, 43 km out in Hardanger, so a city of 290 000 people has nothing inside an hour's drive.

sources.friflyt: https://www.friflyt.no/topptur/skiturer-bergen — a per-area index in the same shape the Hemsedal round was built on: toppunkt, høydemeter, startsted, OPP/NED. It lists three tours.
sources.utno: Individual turforslag. Only the ones whose activity type is skitur are usable; the Kvamskogen hits for Såta and Fotasperrnuten are fottur, with a summer season, and describing a summer path as a ski route is the thing this pipeline exists not to do.

candidates.name: Gullfjellstoppen

published.start: Osavatnet (305 moh) i enden av vegen i Bjørndalen frå rv. 580

trailhead.name: Osavatnet
trailhead.note: The road end on Gullfjellsvegen, 29 m from the mapped way. The register's Osavatnet point is the lake itself.

findings: The register's «Gullfjellet» (60.37313/5.58038) is not the summit. It reads 909,56 m against a published 987, and the highest ground within 700 m of it is 924,83. Gullfjellstoppen is 1,7 km north-north-east, at 60.38756/5.59037, where the raster reads 987,37 and the point API 986,8 — the published figure exactly. Anything that pins this tour to the register point would put the summit 62 m too low and 1,7 km from where it is.
Both intermediate heights Fri Flyt states reproduce: Osavatnet 307,0 against «305 moh», Redningshytta 597,49 against «600 moh».
The trailhead point resolves onto the lake itself (terreng Innsjø). The corridor needs a point on land at the road end before this can be routed.

Every element of Fri Flyt's description reproduces on the mapped ground. The road runs up the valley and passes 538 m south of Svartavatnet — «til høyre for Svartavatnet» is right, and the straight-line reading that made it look wrong was the reading, not the source. Redningshytta measures 596,5 m against «600 moh», and the «liten unnabakke» east of the hut is a real 25 m dip in the line.
The register's Osavatnet point is the lake surface; the trailhead is the road end at 60.37821/5.51921, 307,48 m, 29 m from the mapped Gullfjellsvegen. Fri Flyt's «305 moh» reproduces within 1,6 m.

BLOCKED: the routed line runs over Osavatnet, over Svartavatnet and over a tarn at 766 m. That is the router working as designed — its docstring says «sea is impassable; frozen lakes are not (this is a winter product)» — and flat water is the cheapest ground it knows, so it takes the lake in preference to the road beside it. Twenty-three waypoints pinned along the road at 180 m spacing did not clear it; the line cuts between them.

That assumption does not transfer to this tour. Osavatnet is at 307 m on the coast at the latitude of Bergen, which Fri Flyt itself calls «ikke den mest snøsikre byen», and Svartavatnet is InnsjøRegulert — a regulated lake, drawn down in winter, which is the exact hazard that made Kråkfjellet and Rensfjellet re-routes. A line that sends a paying reader onto that ice is not publishable, whatever the terrain model costs it at.

Two ways forward, and they are a real choice rather than a detail. Either give the router a water cost — correct, contained if only new tours are re-routed, but it makes this tour the only one of 91 built by a different router — or trace the road section from the mapped ways instead of solving it, which is more accurate ground but a different construction from the other 90. Both need saying out loud in the README; neither should be picked quietly.

The router now has an opt-in water cost and it did the job it was added for: the line came off Osavatnet entirely, where it had run for the best part of a kilometre. Length went 7,35 -> 7,51 km and the climb 783 -> 811 m, which is what going round costs.

89 m of 7 514 m is still on water, and two added steering waypoints did not clear it. The Svartavatnet clip is a leg problem rather than a cost problem: the waypoint traced off the mapped road at 60.38561/5.54783 sits north of the lake's south shore, so the leg from it to a point south of the lake crosses the corner whatever the cost. Moving that waypoint, not adding more, is the fix — and it wants a careful read of the shore rather than another blind iteration.

The tour is not publishable at 89 m on water, and 41 m of that is the regulated lake. But it is 1,18% against a line that was previously on the ice for a kilometre, and the remaining fix is corridor geometry with no unknowns left in it.

routed.corridor: 28 waypoints: 23 traced off the mapped road at ~180 m spacing, two steering points, three on the upper mountain
remaining: 41 m clipping the south corner of Svartavatnet (InnsjøRegulert) at vertex 78
48 m over a tarn at 766 m (Innsjø) at vertices 184-185

candidates.name: Såta

published.start: Den innerste parkeringsplassen ved Eikedalen Skisenter på Kvamskogen

findings: The summit resolves to 1260,45 m against a published 1260 — exact.
The register carries «Iendefjell» at the same coordinate as «Såta», which corroborates Fri Flyt's «Såta, som mange kaller Iendafjellet» rather than leaving it as a claim about local usage.
Gain reproduces: 1260,45 − 456,05 = 804 m against a published 800.
Not to be confused with ut.no's Såta on Kvamskogen, which is a 404 m fottur from Mødalsvegen with a year-round season. Different start, different route, and not a ski description.
Rosselandsbotnen resolves onto water. The corridor needs a point on the shore.

candidates.name: Skrott

published.start: Støls-/hyttetunet i Fitjadalen, omtrent åtte kilometer frå Øystese

findings: Summit resolves to 1320,17 m against a published 1320 — exact.
Gain reproduces: 1320,17 − 272,38 = 1048 m against a published 1050.

The route description was only partially retrieved. The ascent via Håsete and a ski hut at about 1000 m is in hand; the descent variants are not, and the corridor should not be drawn from a half-read source.

candidates.name: Tveitakvitingen
candidates.source: ut.no/turforslag/1112154404 — «Skitur til Tveitakvitingen 1299 moh», svært krevende skitur, jan–apr, 9,0 km, 989 høydemeter
findings: Summit resolves to 1298,9 m against a published 1299 — exact.

Held rather than queued for two reasons. The route starts at Furudalen Alpinsenter and follows «preparerte løyper til Mødal»; that has to be checked against terrain class point by point along the line before anything is drawn, the way Trysilfjellet was, because a topptur line that runs in a piste sends a paying reader uphill into ski traffic. And the trailhead did not resolve — the register has no Furudalen on Kvamskogen, only Furedalen, and which of them the source means is not settled.
It also crosses the same massif as Såta — «opp mot Såta i bratte klyv og videre opp Stoveveggen» — so the two tours share ground and should be researched together.

Then re-route Gullfjellstoppen, re-measure, and write its guide in both languages.

Såta: a land point at Rosselandsbotnen and the innermost Eikedalen car park, then the same chain. Overpass was timing out on that box during this round; the trailhead should be pinned to a mapped way the way Osavatnet's was, not read off a tile.
Skrott: read the description in full. Tveitakvitingen: settle the trailhead and check «preparerte løyper» against terrain class.
